A disorder characterized by tearing or disruption of the ovarian tissue.
A disorder characterized by bleeding from the ovary.
A disorder characterized by a sensation of marked discomfort in one side of the abdomen between menstrual cycles, around the time of the discharge of the ovum from the ovarian follicle.
A disorder characterized by a reduction in the strength of the muscles of the pelvic floor.
A disorder characterized by a sensation of marked discomfort in the pelvis.
A disorder characterized by a sensation of marked discomfort in the penis.
A disorder characterized by a sensation of marked discomfort in the area between the genital organs and the anus.

A disorder characterized by premature ovarian failure. Symptoms may include hot flashes, night sweats, mood swings, and a decrease in sex drive. Laboratory findings include elevated luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH.)
A disorder characterized by bleeding from the prostate gland.

A disorder characterized by compression of the urethra secondary to enlargement of the prostate gland. This results in voiding difficulties (straining to void, slow urine stream, and incomplete emptying of the bladder).
A disorder characterized by a sensation of marked discomfort in the prostate gland.
A disorder characterized by a sensation of marked discomfort in the scrotal area.
A disorder characterized by bleeding from the spermatic cord.
A disorder characterized by blockage of the normal flow of the contents of the spermatic cord.
A disorder characterized by bleeding from the testis.
A disorder characterized by abnormal function or appearance of the testis.
A disorder characterized by a sensation of marked discomfort in the testis.
A disorder characterized by an abnormal communication between the uterus and another organ or anatomic site.
A disorder characterized by blockage of the uterine outlet.
A disorder characterized by a sensation of marked discomfort in the uterus.
A disorder characterized by bleeding from the uterus.
A disorder characterized by an abnormal communication between the vagina and another organ or anatomic site.
A disorder characterized by bleeding from the vagina.
A disorder characterized by vaginal secretions. Mucus produced by the cervical glands is discharged from the vagina naturally, especially during the childbearing years.
A disorder characterized by an uncomfortable feeling of itching and burning in the vagina.
A disorder characterized by inflammation involving the vagina. Symptoms may include redness, edema, marked discomfort and an increase in vaginal discharge.
A disorder characterized by blockage of vaginal canal.
A disorder characterized by a sensation of marked discomfort in the vagina.
A disorder characterized by a rupture in the vaginal wall.
A disorder characterized by a narrowing of the vaginal canal.
A disorder characterized by progressive and life-threatening pulmonary distress in the absence of an underlying pulmonary condition, usually following major trauma or surgery.

A disorder characterized by an inflammation of the nasal mucous membranes caused by an IgE-mediated response to external allergens. The inflammation may also involve the mucous membranes of the sinuses, eyes, middle ear, and pharynx. Symptoms include sneezing, nasal congestion, rhinorrhea and itching.
A disorder characterized by cessation of breathing.
A disorder characterized by inhalation of solids or liquids into the lungs.
A disorder characterized by the collapse of part or the entire lung.
A disorder characterized by an abnormal communication between the bronchus and another organ or anatomic site.
A disorder characterized by blockage of a bronchus passage, most often by bronchial secretions and exudates.
A disorder characterized by a narrowing of the bronchial tube.
A disorder characterized by an abnormal communication between a bronchus and the pleural cavity.
A disorder characterized by bleeding from the bronchial wall and/or lung parenchyma.
A disorder characterized by a sudden contraction of the smooth muscles of the bronchial wall.
A disorder characterized by a sudden contraction of the smooth muscles of the bronchial wall or narrowing of the airway. May be manifested as wheezing.
A disorder characterized by milky pleural effusion (abnormal collection of fluid) resulting from accumulation of lymph fluid in the pleural cavity.
A disorder characterized by sudden, often repetitive, spasmodic contraction of the thoracic cavity, resulting in violent release of air from the lungs and usually accompanied by a distinctive sound.
A disorder characterized by an uncomfortable sensation of difficulty breathing.
A disorder characterized by bleeding from the nose.
A disorder characterized by repeated gulp sounds that result from an involuntary opening and closing of the glottis. This is attributed to a spasm of the diaphragm.
A disorder characterized by harsh and raspy voice arising from or spreading to the larynx.
A disorder characterized by a decrease in the level of oxygen in the body.
A disorder characterized by swelling due to an excessive accumulation of fluid in the larynx.
A disorder characterized by an inflammation involving the larynx.
A disorder characterized by ulceration or inflammation involving the mucous membrane of the larynx.
A disorder characterized by blockage of the laryngeal airway.
A disorder characterized by a narrowing of the laryngeal airway.
A disorder characterized by an uncomfortable persistent sensation in the area of the laryngopharynx.
A disorder characterized by paroxysmal spasmodic muscular contraction of the vocal cords.
A disorder characterized by an abnormal communication between the larynx and another organ or anatomic site.
A disorder characterized by bleeding from the larynx.
A disorder characterized by bleeding from the mediastinum.
A disorder characterized by obstruction of the nasal passage due to mucosal edema.
A disorder characterized by a sensation of marked discomfort in the oropharynx.
A disorder characterized by a sensation of marked discomfort in the oropharynx or pain on swallowing.
A disorder characterized by ulceration or inflammation involving the mucous membrane of the pharynx.
A disorder characterized by a narrowing of the pharyngeal airway.
A disorder characterized by a sensation of marked discomfort in the pharyngolaryngeal region.
A disorder characterized by an abnormal communication between the pharynx and another organ or anatomic site.
A disorder characterized by bleeding from the pharynx.
A disorder characterized by a necrotic process occurring in the pharynx.
A disorder characterized by bleeding from the pleural cavity.
A disorder characterized by an increase in amounts of fluid within the pleural cavity. Symptoms include shortness of breath, cough and marked chest discomfort.
A disorder characterized by a sensation of marked discomfort in the pleura.
A disorder characterized by inflammation focally or diffusely affecting the lung parenchyma.
A disorder characterized by abnormal presence of air in the pleural cavity resulting in the collapse of the lung.
A disorder characterized by excessive mucous secretion in the back of the nasal cavity or throat, causing sore throat and/or coughing.
A disorder characterized by expectorated secretions upon coughing.
A disorder characterized by accumulation of fluid in the lung tissues that causes a disturbance of the gas exchange that may lead to respiratory failure.
A disorder characterized by the replacement of the lung tissue by connective tissue, leading to progressive dyspnea, respiratory failure or right heart failure.
A disorder characterized by an abnormal communication between the lung and another organ or anatomic site.
A disorder characterized by an increase in pressure within the pulmonary circulation due to lung or heart disorder.

A disorder characterized by impaired gas exchange by the respiratory system resulting in hypoxia and a decrease in oxygenation of the tissues that may be associated with an increase in arterial levels of carbon dioxide.
A disorder characterized by weight gain, dyspnea, pleural and pericardial effusions, leukocytosis and/or renal failure originally described in patients treated with all-trans retinoic acid.
A disorder characterized by excessive mucous secretions draining from the nose.
A disorder characterized by involvement of the paranasal sinuses.
A disorder characterized by a sensation of marked discomfort in the face, between the eyes, or upper teeth originating from the sinuses.
A disorder characterized by cessation of breathing for short periods during sleep.
A disorder characterized by the involuntary expulsion of air from the nose.
A disorder characterized by marked discomfort in the throat
A disorder characterized by marked discomfort in the throat.
A disorder characterized by a high pitched breathing sound due to laryngeal or upper airway obstruction.
A disorder characterized by an abnormal communication between the trachea and another organ or anatomic site.
A disorder characterized by an inflammation or ulceration involving the mucous membrane of the trachea.
A disorder characterized by a narrowing of the trachea.
A disorder characterized by a change in the sound and/or speed of the voice.
A disorder characterized by a high-pitched, whistling sound during breathing. It results from the narrowing or obstruction of the respiratory airways.
A disorder characterized by a decrease in density of hair compared to normal for a given individual at a given age and body location.
A disorder characterized by an abnormal body smell resulting from the growth of bacteria on the body.
A disorder characterized by inflammation of the skin characterized by the presence of bullae which are filled with fluid.
A disorder characterized by flaky and dull skin; the pores are generally fine, the texture is a papery thin texture.
A disorder characterized by skin which becomes itchy, red, inflamed, crusty, thick, scaly, and/or forms blisters.
A disorder characterized by dry and itchy patches of skin involving the epidermis and superficial dermis and includes some scaling, crusting, or serous oozing.
A disorder characterized by target lesions (a pink-red ring around a pale center).
A disorder characterized by generalized inflammatory erythema and exfoliation. The inflammatory process involves > 90% of the body surface area.
A disorder characterized by generalized inflammatory erythema and exfoliation. The inflammatory process involves >90% of the body surface area.
A disorder characterized by shrinking of adipose tissue.
A disorder characterized by change in hair color or loss of normal pigmentation.
A disorder characterized by a change in the way the hair feels.

A disorder characterized by the presence of excess hair growth in women in anatomic sites where growth is considered to be a secondary male characteristic and under androgen control (beard, moustache, chest, abdomen).
A disorder characterized by excessive sweating.
A disorder characterized by a thickening of the outer layer of the skin.
A disorder characterized by hair density or length beyond the accepted limits of normal in a particular body region, for a particular age or race.
A disorder characterized by reduced sweating.
A disorder characterized by hypertrophy of the subcutaneous adipose tissue at the site of multiple subcutaneous injections of insulin.
A disorder characterized by a change in the nails.
A disorder characterized by a change in the color of the nail plate.
A disorder characterized by loss of all or a portion of the nail.
A disorder characterized by vertical or horizontal ridges on the nails.
A disorder characterized by a sensation of marked discomfort in the skin.
A disorder characterized by redness, marked discomfort, swelling, and tingling in the palms of the hands or the soles of the feet. Also known as Hand-Foot Syndrome.
A disorder characterized by an increase in sensitivity of the skin to light.
A disorder characterized by an intense itching sensation.

A disorder characterized by hemorrhagic areas of the skin and mucous membrane. Newer lesions appear reddish in color. Older lesions are usually a darker purple color and eventually become a brownish-yellow color.
A disorder characterized by an eruption of papules and pustules, typically appearing in face, scalp, upper chest and back.

A disorder characterized by the presence of macules (flat) and papules (elevated). Also known as morbillform rash, it is one of the most common cutaneous adverse events, frequently affecting the upper trunk, spreading centripetally and associated with pruritis.

A disorder characterized by the presence of macules (flat) and papules (elevated). Also known as morbilliform rash, it is one of the most common cutaneous adverse events, frequently affecting the upper trunk, spreading centripetally and associated with pruritis.
A disorder characterized by a sensation of marked discomfort in the skin covering the top and the back of the head.
A disorder characterized by the degeneration and thinning of the epidermis and dermis.
A disorder characterized by darkening of the skin due to excessive melanin deposition.
A disorder characterized by loss of skin pigment (e.g., vitiligo).
A disorder characterized by an area of hardness in the skin.
A disorder characterized by a circumscribed, erosive lesion on the skin.
A disorder characterized by less than 10% total body skin area separation of dermis. The syndrome is thought to be a hypersensitivity complex affecting the skin and the mucous membranes.
A disorder characterized by air in the subcutaneous tissue.
A disorder characterized by local dilatation of small vessels resulting in red discoloration of the skin or mucous membranes.
A disorder characterized by greater than 30% total body skin area separation of dermis. The syndrome is thought to be a hypersensitivity complex affecting the skin and the mucous membranes.
A disorder characterized by an itchy skin eruption characterized by wheals with pale interiors and well-defined red margins.
A disorder characterized by occlusion of an arterial vessel by a blood clot that develops in an artery.

A disorder characterized by leakage of intravascular fluids into the extravascular space. This syndrome is observed in patients who demonstrate a state of generalized leaky capillaries following shock syndromes, low-flow states, ischemia-reperfusion injuries, toxemias, medications, or poisoning. It can lead to generalized edema and multiple organ failure.
A disorder characterized by episodic reddening of the skin, especially face, neck, or chest.
A disorder characterized by a localized collection of blood, usually clotted, in an organ, space, or tissue, due to a break in the wall of a blood vessel.
A disorder characterized by an uncomfortable and temporary sensation of intense body warmth, flushing, sometimes accompanied by sweating upon cooling.
A disorder characterized by a pathological increase in blood pressure.
A disorder characterized by a blood pressure that is below the normal expected for an individual in a given environment.
A disorder characterized by the loss of lymph fluid into the surrounding tissue or body cavity.
A disorder characterized by excessive fluid collection in tissues that causes swelling.
A disorder characterized by a cystic lesion containing lymph.
A disorder characterized by impaired circulation to an extremity.
A disorder characterized by inflammation of the wall of a vein.
A disorder characterized by inflammation of the wall of a peripheral vein associated with an intravenous line.
A disorder characterized by a blood clot and inflammation involving a superficial vein of the extremities.
A disorder characterized by obstruction of the blood flow in the superior vena cava. Signs and symptoms include swelling and cyanosis of the face, neck, and upper arms, cough, orthopnea and headache.
A disorder characterized by occlusion of a vessel by a thrombus that has migrated from a distal site via the blood stream.
A disorder characterized by inflammation involving the wall of a vessel.
A disorder characterized by the inability of the bone marrow to make enough new blood cells.
Anemia resulting from hemolysis.
A finding based on laboratory test results that indicate an increase in number of platelets in a blood specimen.
A disorder characterized by a form of thrombotic microangiopathy with laboratory findings that indicate hemolytic anemia, severe thrombocytopenia, and renal insufficiency/failure.
A disorder characterized by a decrease in production of sex hormones from the gonads.
A disorder characterized by inflammation or destruction of the thyroid gland.
A disorder characterized by the vomiting of blood.
A disorder characterized by the passage of fresh blood per anus, usually in or with stools.
A disorder characterized by black, tarry stools.
A disorder characterized by impaired exocrine pancreatic function usually associated with decreased pancreatic exocrine enzymes production.
A finding of gas in the bowel wall.
A disorder characterized by blockage of the normal flow of the normal flow of bile.
A disorder characterized by inflammation of the liver.
A disorder characterized by donor cells attacking the recipient's organs.

A disorder characterized by the development of a pathological and biochemical hyperinflammatory syndrome characterized by fever, cytopenias, hyperferritinemia, coagulopathy, hypofibrinogenemia and/or transaminitis and is attributable to therapy.
A disorder characterized by an inflammatory process of the meninges of the brain and/or spinal cord.
A disorder characterized by an infectious or inflammatory process involving the meninges and the brain tissue.
A disorder characterized by reactions related to the administration of local or moderate sedation given for a procedure.
A finding of damage to a nerve.
A disorder characterized by bleeding as a result of a biopsy procedure.
A disorder characterized by a systemic manifestation that occurs after the injection of a substance with antigenic properties, administered to activate the immune system.
A finding of damage to an organ or tissue as a result of a procedure.
A finding based on laboratory test results that indicate a decrease in creatinine clearance (CrCl) in a 24-hour urine collection.
A finding based on laboratory test results that indicate a decrease in HDL in a blood specimen.
A finding based on laboratory test results that indicate an increase in LDL in a blood specimen.
A finding based on laboratory test results that indicate an increase in number of neutrophils (ANC) in a blood specimen.
A finding based on laboratory test results that indicate a low concentration of Vitamin D in the blood.
A disorder characterized by increased Hgb A1C that may result in organ damage.
A condition characterized by global decline with weight loss, decreased appetite, poor intake, and/or inactivity.

A potentially fatal complication of treatment in certain molecular subgroups of leukemia characterized by fever, rash, dyspnea and/or hypoxia, pulmonary infiltrates, peripheral edema with rapid weight gain, pleuropericardial effusion, acute renal failure, disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC), bone pain and/or hypotension.
A disorder characterized by a cutaneous tumor that most commonly presents a dome-shaped nodule with a central keratin-filled crater.
A disorder characterized by damage to nerves that control your internal organs.
A disorder characterized by thinking and memory problems that a patient with cancer may have during or after cancer treatment.
A disorder characterized by a thrombus (blood clot) in the brain's venous sinuses leading to swelling and bleeding.
A disorder characterized by a reduction in the strength of the muscles on one side of the body.

A disorder characterized by a pathologic process involving the central nervous system following any immune therapy that results in the activation or engagement of endogenous or infused T cells and/or other immune effector cells. Symptoms or signs can be progressive and may include aphasia, altered level of consciousness, impairment of cognitive skills, motor weakness, seizures, and cerebral edema.
A disorder characterized by inflammation and demyelination of the optic nerve that causes acute, usually monocular, visual loss.
A disorder characterized by localized neurotoxicity related to cellular therapies or other immunotherapies for CNS tumors (TIAN).
A disorder characterized by inflammation of the glomerulus, usually based on renal biopsy.
A disorder characterized by the need to get up at night on a regular basis to urinate.
A disorder characterized by inflammation of the renal tubule and surrounding tissues.

A disorder characterized by the development of oligomenorrhea or amenorrhea for at least 3 consecutive months and serum follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) levels in the menopausal range before age 40. Symptoms of estrogen deficiency may include hot flashes, night sweats, mood swings, and vaginal dryness. Laboratory findings include elevated serum FSH. Other supportive laboratory findings include decreased serum estradiol and anti-Mullerian hormone (AMH) levels.
A disorder characterized by large, red, rounded plaques covered with thicker scales.
A disorder characterized by diffuse erythema and scaling involving > 90% of the body surface area.
A disorder characterized by a symmetric eruption of flat-topped, red or purple papules on the trunk and extremities.
A disorder characterized by an eruption consisting of papules (a small, raised pimple) and vesicles (a small fluid filled blister).
A disorder characterized by the development of nonfollicular, sterile pustules on an erythematous base.
A disorder characterized by occlusion of a vessel by a thrombus that has migrated from a distal site via the blood stream (for example, deep vein thrombosis (DVT), pulmonary embolism (PE), etc.).
